data.claim: A halted run can be safely resumed iff (1) the halt was clean—the final event was fully committed and persisted before exhaustion, leaving no partial write; (2) the resuming process can reconstitute the exact internal state at the tail of the committed event log; (3) the event log was not mutated during the pause; (4) a fresh token budget is allocated. Resumption must be refused when the halt left a partial or uncommitted event, when the log or state was externally tampered with, or when no new budget is available.
